# Mail archiving has separate preparation and copy completion signals

`archiveMessages()` returns an async promise. An empty input resolves to `undefined` before calling `oncomplete`. Otherwise it sets module-wide `gIsArchiving`, awaits destination-folder preparation for each header, registers a folder-notification listener, and starts `processNextBatch()`. Its promise resolves after that launch. It does not wait for all filter and copy callbacks.

`filterBatch()` passes the archiver as `nsIMsgOperationListener`. `onStopOperation()` logs a filter failure but continues to the default archive operation. `continueBatch()` awaits missing subfolders and calls `MailServices.copy.copyMessages()`. `onStopCopy()` advances on success. On failure it clears pending batches, then uses `processNextBatch()` to remove the folder listener and call `oncomplete`. Completion therefore means the archiver stopped processing its queue; the callback has no success/error argument and can also follow a copy failure.

The user command calls `updateNextMessageAfterDelete()`, sets `msgWindow` for undo, and discards the returned promise. The extension `messages.archive()` instead wraps `oncomplete` in a resolve-only promise and discards the preparation promise. It catches synchronous errors in its own wrapper, but an async rejection from `archiveMessages()` is not connected to that outer promise. Empty input also does not call `oncomplete`; the checked schema has no minimum item count, and its collection helper returns an empty map for an empty ID array. The focused extension-empty-input record traces and probes this path.

The browser `archive_messages()` helper waits for `DeleteOrMoveMsgCompleted` or `DeleteOrMoveMsgFailed`; that event wait is distinct from whole-queue completion. The unit test creates a new archiver, assigns `oncomplete` to a deferred resolver, and awaits that resolver before checking source/destination message counts. Those assertions directly cover local and IMAP destination creation, year/month placement, and localized Inbox recreation. They do not directly cover rejected folder preparation, filter failure, concurrent starts, or cancellation.

Ownership: each caller creates its archiver. The instance retains batches, headers, folders, and `msgWindow`. Normal finish removes the registered listener. It sets `_batches` to `null`, then invokes `oncomplete`, then clears `gIsArchiving`. There is no `finally`, cancellation method, or reset path for a rejected awaited folder operation in this module. A callback that throws can prevent the final global-flag reset. A caller starting another archiver synchronously inside `oncomplete` runs before that reset. These are source control-flow observations; real network/UI consequences were not reproduced.
